What we make

Everything you cook with,
made by hand in Italy

Marine Cookers · Techimpex has been building galley appliances in Conegliano, near Venice, for three generations. Gimbaled gas stoves and cookers, induction and radiant electric ranges, built-in hobs and cooktops, ovens, electric grills and barbecues, coffee makers and sinks. Every unit is assembled one at a time in 304 or 316 stainless steel, for sailing yachts, motor yachts and expedition vessels.

01 · Gas

Gimbaled gas cookers with oven

The heart of the range: marine gas stoves with a full oven, gimballed so that the pans stay level while the boat moves. Two, three and four burners, thermocouple safety on every burner, oven doors that stay shut under way. The historic models Classic, XL2, XL3, Top and Mariner remain; alongside them, derived from those same units in an updated version, are the new Marea, Maris, Nauta, Lux and Marina.

See the collection
02 · Gas

Compact gas cookers

For small galleys and tenders, where every centimetre counts. Compact gimballed stoves with one or two burners, built to the same standard as the larger units: marine-grade steel, hand assembly, spare parts available for decades.

See the collection
03 · Electric & Induction

Electric and induction cookers with oven

We put a complete range of radiant electric cookers on the European market at a time when cooking aboard meant gas and nothing else. In 2015 we put into production the first collection of gimballed induction cookers with oven, designed for the sea rather than adapted from a domestic kitchen. Eleven models, from Orizzonte and Tolomeo to Nobilis, Altalux and Granlux.

See the collection
04 · Electric & Induction

Built-in electric cooktops

The widest collection of built-in marine cooktops in Europe: induction and glass-ceramic, one to four zones, flush into the worktop. Patented cooking systems that draw less from the batteries and hold temperature while the vessel moves, which is why owners on long passages choose them over domestic hobs.

See the collection
05 · Gas

Built-in gas cooktops

The pure flame, flush into the galley. Marine gas hobs in one, two, three and four burners, with safety valves and pan holders designed to grip in a seaway. For galleys where the oven sits separately, or where the flame is simply preferred.

See the collection
06 · Ovens

Built-in gas and electric ovens

Ovens that bake at sea, in a range of sizes, in gas or electric. Built to be installed on their own, above or below the cooktop, in stainless steel throughout, with doors and seals engineered for the movement and the salt.

See the collection
07 · Grills

Marine electric grills

Electric grills for boats, built in or rail mounted, with armoured or glass-ceramic elements in marine-grade 304 or 316 stainless steel. Flameless cooking on deck, with no gas bottle and no charcoal: what most modern yards now specify, and what a growing number of marinas require.

See the collection
08 · Grills

Marine electric barbecues

Electric barbecues and BBQs with a cooking lid, for the cockpit and the flybridge, rail mounted or built in on a boat. The lid holds the heat and the smoke where they belong, so that a barbecue at anchor does not become a problem for the boat alongside.

See the collection
09 · Grills

Gas grills

For owners who want the flame on deck. Marine gas grills in stainless steel, with the same safety systems as the galley appliances and the same finish, so that the boat reads as one piece.

See the collection
10 · Classic

Antiche Cambuse · galleys for classic yachts

Bespoke stoves and galleys for vintage and classic yachts, made one at a time by hand. Brass, copper and polished steel, drawn from the original plans or from photographs, with modern safety hidden inside a period form. Restoration work that the yards bring to us because almost nobody still does it.

See the collection
11 · Galley

Coffee makers

The Italian espresso ritual carried to the open sea. Built for the movement and for the electrical system of a boat, because a proper coffee at anchor is not a detail for the people who live aboard.

See the collection
12 · Galley

Sinks and accessories

Stainless steel marine sinks, pan holders that hold a pot at thirty degrees of heel, and the accessories that turn a set of appliances into a working galley.

Heritage

Crafted where Italy meets the sea

Venezia · Italy · Three Generations of Italian Steel Craft

01 · Origin

Born where hills meet the Adriatic

Techimpex - Marine Cookers embodies the finest Italian tradition in the design and manufacture of cookers for sailing yachts and prestigious vessels. Our headquarters are in Conegliano, at the foot of the Venetian hills · a land celebrated for wine, cuisine, and manufacturing excellence.

From a territory so deeply connected to culinary culture, it was only natural that a company specialised in yacht cookers would be born here. And who better than Italians · undisputed masters of gastronomy · to design instruments for cooking at sea?

"Steel, shaped by hand · refined by the sea." Marine Cookers · Techimpex

02 · Inox Valley

Steel, craft and legacy

The artisans who build our cookers, in the workshops of our district and at our own bench, are the latest link in a chain of know-how passed from one generation to the next, born in a small steel workshop and handed down ever since.

That heritage lives on in the Inox Valley, home to legendary names such as Zoppas and Zanussi, and in the maritime culture of the Serenissima Republic of Venice, distilled into cookers refined down to the smallest detail.

Our bodies are built from heavy-gauge stainless steel · components turned and milled from solid metal to outlast the boat itself. Oven doors carry hinges of the highest quality: on models such as Lux and Orizzonte they are solid stainless steel, made to our own design. And on Orizzonte, Tolomeo and Mega Grill the knobs too are solid steel, milled and turned from billet. It is the culture of the professional kitchen, carried out to sea.

Heavy duty

Heavy duty, down to the last detail

Heavy duty is not a slogan: it is how every part is bent, turned and welded to our specification. Generous thicknesses, machine-shop tolerances, finishes that stand up to salt and to time.

At sea a cooker is under the same strain as in the brigade of a busy restaurant: heat, salt, motion, one service after another. So we build it by the rules of a professional kitchen · components cut from solid, turned and milled, welded joints, nothing left to chance.

And we do not work alone. Between the Piave, the Pordenone plain and the Venetian lagoon lies a true triangle of steel: the industrial excellences of Veneto and Friuli, where some of the finest professional cooking equipment on the planet is born. It is the same know-how that fires the brigades of three-star restaurants and the kitchens of luxury hospitality, from Armani to Bulgari, and that we carry, unchanged, on board.

We draw on the whole district: many of our components come from firms that work for the professional world alone. Burners and heating elements are often developed together with us · like this patented heating element, with a heavy-gauge stainless steel frame and special insulation, made with a leading manufacturer that works exclusively for the top-tier professional world.

03 · La Serenissima

Where Venice set sail

Our cultural roots are tied to the maritime tradition of the Serenissima Republic of Venice · one of history's most influential naval powers. Just as Venice united culture, technique and mastery of the seas, we unite refined design and technical reliability to create unique cookers for those who love the sea.

We work with some of Italy's most distinguished designers, including Marco Zito, professor of design at IUAV Venice · one of Italy's most prestigious design institutes.

"From the lagoon of Venice to the open ocean · our cookers follow the sea." La Serenissima heritage

04 · Innovation

Firsts that defined the sector

A meeting with Luca Bassani, founder of Wally, inspired an electric designer nautical cooker for sailing yachts · created at a time when modern design had not yet touched the aesthetics of contemporary sailing vessels. This became HORIZON4, still an icon of the sector.

Always for Wally, we developed a fully aluminium lightweight cooker. And for Perini Navi, we engineered a special cooker with a unique reverse-gimballing system.

05 · Many Souls

Many souls, one workshop

An electric barbecue for a motor superyacht and a gas cooker for a charter boat have nothing in common: different constraints, different materials, a different way of cooking on board altogether. We build both. Alongside them: electric grills for dayboats, our most advanced models for Mediterranean cruising and our most heavily reinforced for bluewater ocean passages, the classic finishes of vintage yachts, cookers drawn from scratch for a single hull.

This is not a range assembled to fill a catalogue. It is what happens when you have never told a shipyard that something cannot be done.

06 · Our Clients

Trusted by the world's finest yards

Our cookers have been trusted for decades by the world's most important shipyards, renowned distributors, and private owners. From modern Solaris yachts to classic vessels like William Fife III's Latifa (1936), from Giovanni Soldini's Elmo's Fire to the yachts of celebrated artists, Formula One champions, internationally renowned statesmen, and leading figures from the worlds of business and finance.

A tradition that continues today with Cantiere del Pardo, ICE Yachts, Sunseeker, Sanlorenzo, and many others · wherever excellence at sea demands excellence in the galley.

Case studies

Our cookers, on real boats

Shipyards, owners and refits: what we built, and why it was built that way.

Off-grid Cooking · Research & Development

Energy efficiency
is our signature

Whether at sea or on expedition, a galley demands dedicated engineering that removes the strain on the electrical system and guarantees constant performance and safety. Our appliances are designed to redefine industry standards, built around absolute efficiency and structural excellence.

I Build & Hygiene

Steel-grade robustness, impeccable hygiene

The first pillar of a true off-grid professional galley is solidity. Our appliances are built like a tank, engineered to withstand the most extreme stresses on the open sea and the roughest terrain.

This strength is paired with a rigorous approach to hygiene. Our oven cavities are built in polished stainless steel, not brushed: there is no abrasive grain in which residues can lodge, so surfaces are exceptionally quick and easy to clean.

II Thermal Insulation

Advanced insulation, efficiency by design

Energy efficiency is where we refuse to compromise. We go beyond standard insulation: our ovens and appliances combine multiple insulation systems, from the thermal stability of rock wool to engineered sandwich panels built with the most innovative and technologically advanced materials available on the global market.

The result keeps thermal dispersion to a minimum, retains heat optimally and delivers a drastic energy saving that relieves the onboard batteries from continuous recharge cycles.

III Gas & Electric

Professional performance, at its peak

We don't just contain consumption: we maximise cooking performance to achieve the gastronomic results that made Italian cooking famous worldwide.

  • Gas systems. Our models feature high-efficiency burners developed together with leading names in professional catering.
  • Electric. In the marine sector we built a complete range of electric marine cookers at a time when cooking aboard meant gas alone.
  • Induction (2015). In 2015 we put into production the first collection of gimballed induction cookers for sailing and motor yachts; the line reached the market at the beginning of 2016.
IV Marine Induction

Marine induction is not home induction

Cooking with induction in the middle of the ocean or in the desert requires specific measures compared to a domestic setting. Drawing on years of experience and leadership, we forged a strategic partnership with one of Europe's leading manufacturers of induction components, developing flexible and unique solutions, available in custom variants too.

  • Structural resistance. Electrical components engineered specifically to withstand constant vibration and mechanical shock.
  • Intelligent generator management. Powerful inductors and bridge systems paired with electronic configurations that regulate and modulate power fluidly, drastically reducing stress on inverters and generators and preventing the sudden trips of onboard safety systems.
  • Extreme optimisation (the 1 kW limit). Our R&D division reached an extraordinary milestone, creating optimised models capable of running an entire hob within an absolute limit of just 1 kW.
V The Italian Method

The Italian art of intelligent cooking

True energy efficiency is not limited to electronics: it extends to the very way food is prepared in demanding contexts. Our Research & Development department studied the culture of cooking away from home, going beyond mere technical performance.

We researched and refined a whole set of cooking techniques optimised for boats and off-grid vehicles, capable of drastically reducing the use of resources and energy during preparation. Being Italian, we took the research as far as the selection and combination of particular raw ingredients, chosen specifically to make thermal processes faster and more efficient. This union of gastronomic method and strategic ingredients cuts real consumption while elevating the final quality.

OCEANO Bluewater Cookers
Ocean Passages · Since the Beginning

Cookers built
for the ocean

A cooker built for an ocean passage has almost nothing in common with one built for coastal cruising. Two different worlds, and in part incompatible ones.

I Why It Differs

Weeks at sea change every decision

Many of our cookers can be built in variants modified for bluewater use: the models that offer it carry the Oceano Bluewater badge. And in any case, every product in the range can be customised into a dedicated reinforced variant.

We have built cookers for ocean passages since the very beginning, and there are today literally thousands of Techimpex cookers at sea aboard yachts of every kind.

Crossing an ocean means living for weeks with limited power, constant motion, salt air and no prospect of assistance. Every construction choice that ashore is a detail becomes, on board, the difference between cooking and not cooking.

II At Sea

The boats that ask the most

Among them is the XXL3 built to measure for Elmo’s Fire, the yacht of the great Italian offshore sailor Giovanni Soldini.

And there is Latifa. An ocean racer in the fullest sense of the term: designed by William Fife III and launched in Scotland in 1936 by the yard of William Fife & Son, she is counted among the finest the great Scottish designer ever drew, and by many as the finest of them all. For her refit we built a cooker in the Classic variant, made entirely to measure: special burners, an oversized oven, a reinforced one-piece steel grate cut from solid, and gimbal pivots of exceptional strength.

The XXL3 and the LATIFA model, which takes its name from the yacht herself, are only two examples of cookers reinforced or customised for extreme ocean use. The specification is the starting point, and from there the cooker is built around the boat it will live on.

III Structure

Built as one piece

The oven cavity is assembled by interlocking joints rather than by fastening separate panels. The result behaves as a single monolithic body, and it is what gives these models their exceptional rigidity under sustained working loads.

Stainless steels are drawn from the top of the range, AISI 316L included: the molybdenum-bearing grade, the one that resists chlorides.

IV Safety On Board

A cooker you can trust in a seaway

  • Heat-resistant knobs. A dedicated variant for long cooking sessions in a closed galley.
  • Door handles of dedicated design. Shaped to reduce the risk of injuring yourself against them as the vessel moves.
  • Reinforced pot holders. Sized to keep pans in place through a working seaway.
  • Oversized door lock. The oven stays shut whatever the boat is doing.
  • Ultra-reinforced gimbal variants. Heavier brackets and pivots than the standard range, for continuous motion over weeks rather than hours.
V Cooking & Power

Cooking well on limited power

  • Dedicated heating elements. Not the ones fitted to the standard range, and more capable.
  • Induction hobs developed for life on board. Not standard modules: power management is designed to reduce cycling and the strain it places on inverter and generator.
  • Ovens adapted to ocean passages. Specific heating elements and a heat management approach conceived for limited power.

Further bluewater solutions are available on request, or can be developed together with the client. It is the work we have always done for shipyards and owners, one boat at a time.

VI Galileo Collection

When you want to go further still

Everything described so far is the standard range built in its Bluewater version: cookers that are already exceptionally sturdy, aboard thousands of boats that cross oceans, and for most of those boats they are the right answer.

Galileo goes further again. It is a small collection of cookers with exceptional performance and a great many solutions found nowhere else, made for owners who want the most that can be had, in every sense of the word, when the passage is a long one. It does not replace the Bluewater variants: it stands beyond them, for a different demand.

SINKS Made to Measure
Sinks · Any Dimension

Cut to the
millimetre

Every sink we build is made to measure. There is no list of standard sizes to choose from: you give us the opening, and the basin is drawn around it.

I How They Are Made

Professional processes, marine dimensions

These sinks come from the world of professional kitchens: the same forming, the same welds, the same tolerances. We build them with a zero radius in the corners, or with a wider radius where a softer line suits the galley better. The choice is yours, and it takes nothing away from the strength of the basin.

II What Goes With Them

Boards, colanders, and whatever else is needed

On board a sink is rarely only a sink: every surface has to do more than one job. Ours take chopping boards, colanders, draining trays and other accessories that rest on the rim and turn the basin into worktop when it is not in use.

Give us the opening, and we build the basin around it.

SOAPSTONE Valtellina
Cooking Accessories

Soapstone from
the Valtellina

Our ovens are Italian ovens: built for static cooking, with the heat rising from below. It is an old choice, and it is the one that makes everything else on this page possible.

I The Static Oven

Heat that comes from below

In a static oven heat is not blown: it radiates. It rises from the floor of the chamber and wraps the food slowly, without drying the surface before the inside is ready. This is how Italian home ovens and bread ovens cook, and it is why in an oven like this the rise carries on through the first minutes instead of stopping, the crust forms where crust belongs, and what should stay soft underneath stays soft. It allows the long braise, the roast that keeps its juices, the gratin that closes on top without drying the filling, and pastry, which a current of air would ruin.

II In the Galley

What comes out of an oven like this

Bread, pizza and focaccia, which take their double nature of crust and crumb from static heat. Roasts and braises, cooked long and low. Fish in salt crust or in paper, where what matters is heat that wraps rather than heat that dries. Bakes, soufflés and vegetable flans, which a fan would collapse. Short pastry, sweet leavened doughs, meringues left to dry for hours in an oven almost switched off. And whole roasted vegetables, which want time and not haste.

III The Accessory

The advantages do not stop there

Having the heat arrive from below made it possible to introduce an accessory unlike any other into our ovens: the stone. There are two of them, and they come from two different Italies. Lava stone is volcanic basalt, quarried from the old flows of Etna, in Sicily. Soapstone comes instead from the thousand-year-old quarries of the Valtellina and the Valchiavenna, in the province of Sondrio. Two rocks opposite in history and in temperament, and good for two different things.

IV The Soapstone

Five thousand years of quarries

It is not born of fire but of pressure: deep rocks, rich in magnesium, slowly transformed in the roots of the Alps. What comes out is a metamorphic rock of talc, chlorite and magnesite, matt green, soft enough to be turned on a lathe and yet refractory. The conditions that form it are so particular that in Italy it is found almost nowhere else. In the quarries of Alpe Pirlo, Val Giumellino and Valbrutta, above Chiesa in Valmalenco and Lanzada, it has been cut since the Neolithic: Pliny the Elder already mentions it in his Naturalis Historia, and by the sixteenth century the pots turned on water-driven lathes were going down the valley to be sold across Italy. Those same pots are still in use, and the same slabs sit in the ovens of Italian restaurants that hold stars. It cooks gently and evenly: it is the stone of bread, of pizza, of focaccia, of the long bake.

V The Lava Stone

Basalt from the volcanoes

It is magma that stopped. Cooling in the open air along the slopes, the flow becomes basalt: a dark, dense rock full of microscopic pores, made of plagioclase, pyroxenes and olivine. It is hard where soapstone is soft, and it takes high temperatures and sudden changes without cracking. That is why it is the stone of the grill made indoors: steaks, fish, vegetables over fierce heat. The porous surface is naturally non-stick and keeps the fat away from the food.

VI On Board

One pan less, one flywheel more

Cooking a steak on the stone, inside the oven, means not having a searing pan on the cooktop while the boat moves: no spitting fat, no smoke in the saloon, less risk. And the stone, once hot, is a remarkable thermal flywheel: it holds heat for a long time and gives it back slowly, so the oven works less to keep its temperature. On board, where every watt and every kilo of gas is counted, that is not a detail.

VII When It Was Magic

The stone that took the poison out

For centuries these stones were believed to hold powers. At Piuro, in the Valchiavenna, soapstone pots were said to neutralise poison while the food boiled, which is how they ended up on the tables of those who had enemies. Fat kept in those vessels was said to last for decades without turning, the stone was said never to wear away, the fire was said to have no hold on it. It was the talc and the chlorite, the porosity, the slowness with which heat enters and leaves. But whoever was cooking did not know that, and called it the magic stone.

The same rock that five thousand years ago became a cooking pot now goes into an oven that sails.

The product lines presented on this site do not always coincide with those handled by the dealers and wholesalers who stock their spare parts: despite sharing a name, the products can differ substantially. The same model may also vary from one distributor to another in finishes, materials, burners, accessories and optional equipment, differences that are reflected in the price.

Write to us
Service · Spare Parts

Spare Parts

Every Marine Cookers appliance is built to last, and to be serviced for decades. Tell us the model you own and we will point you to the exact parts it needs.

The quickest way to start is to send us a photo of your cooker. We will identify the model at once and confirm the correct spares. A picture taken with your phone is more than enough.

Our technical service is open seven days a week. Write to us and you will receive a reply within a few hours, then a quote from the distributor for your country, usually within a day.

How to order
Identify the part you need by browsing or searching the catalogue below. Each entry includes a reference code and, where available, an original photograph of the component. To place a request, write to info@marinecookers.com quoting the reference code, the photograph (or its link) and the model of your cooker. Our office will reply with availability, lead time and shipping arrangements.

Venezia · Italy · Three Generations of Italian Steel Craft

Electric Cookers
for the Sea

Precision engineering and artisanal craft, designed to perform at the highest level on the world's finest yachts.

Scroll
The Collection · Electric Cookers with Oven

Electric Cooking
at Sea
Since the Early 2000s

01 · The Origins
An Italian workshop and the electric galley

The engineers and partners who work on the development of our products introduced a range of electric cookers with oven for yachts in the early 2000s. Rooted in Conegliano and in a craft tradition handed down through three generations, that work opened a category at a time when cooking on board still meant gas. Those cookers are aboard a great many yachts around the world, and many are still in service today.

02 · Radiant & Induction
From radiant plates to induction · more than ten years on

As the natural evolution of that work, the company has been building gimballed induction cookers with oven for yachts for more than ten years. This collection is distinguished above all by exceptional sturdiness: it is built for boats that stay out, where a repair is not an option.

03 · Aesthetic Rigor
Class, restraint, and technical sophistication

Every electric cooker in this collection is defined by a rigorous aesthetic standard. Clean geometry, refined materials, and meticulous proportions place these appliances at the intersection of industrial design and artisanal craft. The result is a product that belongs · visually and functionally · in the galleys of the world's most demanding naval architecture firms and the most discerning private owners.

04 · Handcrafted Excellence
Meticulous craftsmanship, one unit at a time

Each unit is assembled by hand in Conegliano, in the heart of the Treviso industrial district · a region with a deep-rooted tradition in precision metalwork and mechanical craftsmanship. Marine-grade stainless steel, corrosion-resistant finishes, and components engineered for the harshest sea conditions reflect a manufacturing philosophy where performance and durability are never compromised.

"Trusted by Ferretti, Sunseeker, Sanlorenzo, and Cantiere del Pardo, because when excellence is the standard, the galley cannot be an afterthought."
